phase: Phase 2: Green — the updates and the lock file
summary: The r6 score-difference and stale-worktree concerns are resolved. Two shell checks remain unsafe: an early npm ci failure can be ignored, and the SKIP check masks its own failure.
blocking_findings: The two npm-ci chains do not reliably stop when the first install fails. Under `set -e`, a failing command before the final command in an `&&` list is exempt from errexit; the enclosing `&&` list can return nonzero without ending the script. A shell probe confirmed that `set -euo pipefail; (false && true) && (true && true); printf continued` prints `continued` and exits 0. If `npm ci` fails in a harness worktree, later commands can still proceed. Check each `npm ci` command with an explicit failure handler or a separately tested command. Evidence: measure/tracks/deps_refresh/plan.md:293-294.

The SKIP guard always succeeds because `|| true` catches both the expected no-match from grep and the failure from the error handler. When grep finds `SKIP`, the block executes `exit 1`, then the trailing `|| true` runs and masks that status. Replace this with a guard that fails only when grep finds a match. Evidence: measure/tracks/deps_refresh/plan.md:312.
nonblocking_findings: The A/B still uses one unpinned system Chrome version and one sequential pair. The plan records this timing risk and records the Chrome version. A single pair cannot measure score variance across runs.
evidence: F1 withdrawn: task 3.1 now says any score difference stops and returns to the PM; it no longer retries only the new side. Evidence: plan.md:261-263 and 332-334.
